_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
1/10 2:47PM - Afternoon, Stratton! Tonight, forecasts are calling for some mixed precipitation consisting of snow, freezing rain, and sleet transitioning into snow showers with a possible drizzle into the morning. With the dynamic weather, surface conditions will be similar to today with expected lift and terrain delays. We plan on having 65 ways down, all of which are set to receive fresh stripes early in the morning. 13 lifts are set to spin at 8:30AM with anticipated wind and weather related delays. Additionally, there will be no early access tomorrow due to weather conditions. Be sure to tune in frequently for updates to come.

Forecasted warmer temperatures have temporarily put snow guns on hold. Once cold temperatures return, snowmaking, resurfacing, and expansion into Sun Bowl will be in full force with the tentative start being Sunday evening. A brief warm up and freeze cycle is nothing new for our Operations Team, who will continue working around the clock to deliver the best possible conditions. 

Looking ahead to MLK weekend, forecasts are trending in a promising direction with snow on the radar. It’s never too early to start those snow dances! 

Rest up, sharpen those edges, and we will see you bright and early!

Safety Tip: More riders around you means less speed and more awareness.

Join Quiver and access premium skis at top resorts with no hassle; just the right gear for the right conditions. Reserve 24 hours in advance at skiquiver.com and use our limited time Stratton Exclusive code, “Quiver30” for 30% off any Quiver product (seasonal membership, pay-as-you-go membership, and daily rate). Your skis will be waiting slopeside–pickup details will be provided prior to your trip.

Discover the thrill of skiing or snowboarding with Stratton Mountain's Learn to Ski or Ride Program. This step-by-step program is designed to help you master the slopes—and reward you with a 25/26 Stratton Select Pass, to ride out the rest of the season, upon completion.

Looking to progress this season? Stratton’s Camps and Clinics offer targeted skill development, expert coaching, and a strong sense of community for skiers and snowboarders. From women’s programs to freestyle, snowboard, and advanced clinics, each offers a supportive, goal-focused environment to help you make the most of the season, with programs offered all throughout the winter. 

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: Welcome to the weekend! Brace yourself for bell-to-bell sunshine and pleasant packed powder skiing. Temperatures will start the day in the mid-teens and rise into the mid-20s by this afternoon. The year is off to a great start with 5 feet of new snow since January 1. Most of our frontside terrain is now open, along with Summit Express, serving 50+ open trails. To reach Summit you must take the Sunrise chairlift; no access to Summit is available from Apex Express. Do not duck ropes into closed terrain. Serious hazards exist beyond our ropelines and you’ll lose your pass for 30 days or more at all Ikon Pass resorts. Our second Nordic Nights of the season takes place tonight at the Solitude Nordic & Snowshoe Center. Fresh snow and clear skies will make this a night to remember!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Laurie with your 5 am snow report for Saturday, January 10th. Remember, the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  
It’s a powder day in the Boat! At Mid Mountain, we’ve had 5 new inches of snow in the past 24 hours, with 0 inches falling since the mountain closed yesterday.  
At the Summit, we’ve had 6 new inches of snow in the past 24 hours, with 1 inch falling since the mountain closed yesterday. 
Our Mid mountain base is 37 inches, the temperature is 8 degrees, the winds are 6 miles per hour from the NW, with cloudy skies.
The Summit base is 53 inches, the temperature is 0 degrees, the winds are 18 miles per hour from the WNW, and it’s currently snowing.
The base temperature is 5 degrees. 
We will be skiing and riding on 19 lifts, 111 runs, and 1549 acres on Powder snow. 

Join us tonight for Comedy on the Mountain—ride the Steamboat Gondola up to Thunderhead Lodge for live music and a full stand-up set from acclaimed comedian Joe Stapleton. Cozy up with good company, stunning alpine views, a full bar, and light bites for a hilarious night out in Ski Town, U.S.A. Tickets required head to steamboat.com/comedy to purchase. 

Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more. 
If you are thinking of exploring outside the ski area boundaries, and don’t know exactly where you are going, don’t go. 
Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Saturday, January 10, 2026 9:30 AM – The Village Gondola is now open. It's a crisp start to the day with calm winds and partly cloudy skies. We’re finally seeing a warm-up, with temperatures climbing into the 30s later today. 23 lifts are expected, conditions permitting. Pockets of wind buff are waiting in protected terrain, and groomers are shaping up soft and smooth. With deep snow still in play, stay aware, keep your crew close, and give tree wells plenty of space. 

Conditions and Visibility: Clear skies with calm winds. It's cold this morning, with warmer temps in the 30s later today. Partly cloudy skies may make it feel colder. Packed powder base, with soft snow on top.
Lift status: 23 lifts are expected to operate, conditions permitting.  
Safety: Please avoid tree wells and try to land feet first when falling. Always ski and ride in a group and keep them in sight. Learn more about tree wells and Snow Immersion Suffocation. Please give heavy machinery space. Our on-mountain emergency hotline is: 760.934.0611 
Road Conditions: Expect snow and ice covered surfaces, so please drive with caution and watch for slick spots. Check our Road Conditions page for the latest status.
_inspectorSnowReport.SafetyReport: Ski with a buddy and avoid tree wells. Emergency Hotline: 760.934.0611

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Saturday January 10, 2026 -- 7:30AM

Chilly temps this morning with partly cloudy skies. Temps will rise to the 30s today and expected to stay warm throughout the weekend. Expect all lifts on time today.  There are still pockets of snow in the trees looking to get tracked so bring a friend and explore all types of terrain June has to offer! Plan for the temps to continue rising throughout the weekend so don't forget to pack your sunscreen!

Remember -- snow is deep and ice is present. Ride with friends and avoid tree wells on the mountain--take the time to educate yourself on how to safely ride in these conditions before heading to the mountain. Be cautious on walkways and roadways. With these colder temps the ground is very slippery; the roads are icy and the 395 might require chains. Be prepared! 

Check out our safety and conduct page here and road conditions here

1/10/26 4 PM Update: Winds have calmed a bit and the night is prime for some skiing and riding! Quicksilver, Gold Hills, and Discovery are open until 8pm tonight, and every Thursday - Sunday. As a reminder, parking reservations are not required for afternoon arrivals, at which point parking becomes first come, first served. Be sure to join us for Happy Hour at Rafters from 3pm-5pm today for live music, games and specials, as well as a Seattle Kraken watch party with puck drop at 4pm! We have another busy day tomorrow and would like to remind everyone to allow extra time getting to the mountain. Have a great evening!

Snow conditions are primo mountain-wide after over 2 feet of new snow fell with this week's storm, and you can still find some stashes of that untouched powder! Though be aware, early season conditions and unmarked hazards still exist. Please respect the ropes and closed areas, and we always recommend skiing and riding with a partner- have a plan and check in often. Take a moment to read more on our newly revamped Mountain Safety page!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
January 10th, 1:36 PM
Good afternoon riders and skiers! Fresh corduroy and cooler temps set the stage for a firm and fast day on the slopes. Tomorrow's forecast calls for cloudy skies with similar temperatures in the high 20s to low 30s at both the base and summit. Strong winds could affect lift operations tomorrow. Groomers will be out tonight tackling the firm and frozen trails from last night's freeze. Look forward to top-tier groomers, along with firm, variable conditions on natural terrain. All terrain off Bravo, Heaven's Gate, and Valley House is for advanced skiers and riders due to variable conditions. Snowmaking continues to be on pause until temps become cooperative.

We’ll be getting down on over 450 skiable acres served by 15 lifts and 106 open trails, 30 of which received fresh corduroy overnight. Castlerock and North Lynx lifts will be turning tomorrow from 9:00 AM - 3:45 PM. All ungroomed and natural terrain is suggested for experts only as base coverage has become thin and conditions are variable. Inverness trail is reserved today for racing events. Check out Gate House terrain for some mellow and easy-going groomers, perfect for the kiddos, beginners, or anyone avoiding the icy conditions.

Operations have switched to weekend hours: GMX, Super Bravo, and Heaven’s Gate kick things off, loading at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. This weekend, Ikon Pass holders can score some early turns during Ikon Early Ups. Super Bravo will be loading at 7:30 AM for Ikon pass holders before opening to the public at 8:00 AM. Sugarbush offers a wide range of freestyle parks, whether you’re just starting out or training for competitions, we’ve got you covered. At Mt. Ellen, Riemergasse offers 80 of the finest features on the East Coast, while Lincoln Peak is home to two mini parks featuring 12 creative elements. Sugar Run made its season debut earlier this week with 27 features including 3 jumps, bringing our total feature count to 119!

Sharpen Your Swing This Winter! Join PGA Pro Roger King Jan 12th from 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM at the SIM Suites in the SHaRC for exclusive winter golf lessons. Using state-of-the-art simulators, you'll get personalized tips and real-time feedback to improve your swing, accuracy, and overall game. Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill routes are open at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen, check out our uphill travel policy for more info.

Bonjour Tremblant!

Due to windy conditions forecasted for today and an ice layer covering the mountain this morning, our teams are hard at work to prepare the terrain safely. In these conditions, grooming and trail preparation take significantly more time than usual.

As a result, many trails will open progressively throughout the morning, with the Soleil side making its comeback today—slopes on this side will also open gradually as conditions improve. Despite everything, First Tracks will still be available to enjoy on the North Side! Please be careful on the slopes, as conditions will be very variable across the mountain terrain today.

We invite you to check this webpage regularly for the latest updates as terrain openings evolve. Thank you for your patience and understanding, and have a great day on the mountain!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users.
 
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
_inspectorSnowReport.SafetyReport: This Saturday, conditions will be windy all day, and an ice layer is covering the mountain this morning, making skiing conditions very variable across the entire resort. Many trails, including the terrain parks, will therefore open progressively throughout the morning. Despite this, the Soleil sides is making its comeback today! Please ski carefully and enjoy your day on the slopes!
